sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 13.12.2022 passed in MACC No.8101073/2016 by the XXt h Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.5,88,100/- has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
3. As per the appellant, on 30.03.2016 he along with his brother was going on his motorcycle from his field to his house.

When they reached Indore Nemabar road in front of Sardar Daba, respondent No.2 drove Eicher vehicle bearing registration No.MP- 09-GF-3111 which was owned by respondent No.3 and was insured with respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against their motorcycle as a result of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9481 2 MA-3836-2024 which they fell down.
Due to the accident the appellant suffered grievous injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.

4. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims Sobhagya Singh vs Union India Insurance Co. Ltd. on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188179706/
1 tribunal for award of compensation to him for the injuries suffered by him in the accident.

sentences.text: The application was contested by respondents by filing their written statements to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.
5. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that his income which has been assessed at Rs.5,000/- per month, is grossly low.
At the time of the accident, appellant was aged about 48 years and was doing agricultural work on his own land and was having sufficient income.
The same could not have been taken as has been taken by the claims tribunal.

It is further submitted that due to accident the right leg of the appellant was amputated below the knee and the permanent disability certificate which has been issued by the doctor stated his permanent disability to be 50% but the claims tribunal has illegally assessed the same at 40%.
It is further submitted that for transportation, attendant and special diet amount has been awarded as a whole instead of separately.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1/insurance company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9481 3 MA-3836-2024 by the Claims Tribunal to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. In his statement before the claims tribunal the appellant had categorically stated that he was doing agricultural work in his own field.
It could not have been expected from him to produce any document as regards his income.

In any case he ought to have been considered at least to be an unskilled labourer and considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2016 his income in view of the applicable guidelines are taken at Rs.6,525/- per month.
In the accident the appellant had suffered amputation of his right leg below his knee.
In the permanent disability certificate issued by the medical board Exhibit P/7 it has been categorically stated that his permanent disability is 50%.

The same is in consonance with the schedule appended to the Employee's Insurance Act,
1923.
His permanent disability, hence ought to have been taken at 50% and not 40% as has been done by the claims tribunal.
For transportation, attendant and special diet he deserves to be awarded amount individually.

9. For the permanent disablement suffered by the appellant, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.6,525/- +
25% future prospects of rise in income which would be Rs.8,156/- per month i.e.Rs.97,872/- per annum.
The multiplier of 13 is applied correctly and by taking permanent disability at 50% the amount under this head comes to Rs.6,36,168/-.
For transportation, attendant and special diet the appellant deserves to be awarded a sum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9481 4 MA-3836-2024 Rs.10,000/- each.

His loss of income for three months, would hence the Rs.19,575/-
.
The amount awarded to the appellant under the other heads is proper.

sentences.text: The appellant is entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.8,63,843/- to him by way of compensation whereas the claims tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs.5,88,100/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the amount in compensation in the sum of Rs.2,75,743/- which shall be paid to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
11. The direction of the claims tribunal for the insurance company to pay the compensation amount and to recover the same from the owner and driver of the vehicle is maintained.
The appellant has valued this appeal Rs.2 Lakhs whereas the enhancement in the amount of compensation has been made in the sum of Rs.2.75.743/-.
The appellant would hence be required to pay the requisite Court fees on the additional enhanced amount of Rs.75,743/- which shall be paid by him within a period of two months from today.
In case the Court fees is not paid as aforesaid, this enhanced amount of Rs.75,743/- shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
12. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
